limits: Ordinary run variance is acceptable; percentages alone do not establish a regression.
Windows native performance comparisons are unavailable because the current workload monitor requires POSIX process enumeration.
Native scenarios start after an active photo and the graphics device have loaded. They do not measure cold process startup or screen scanout.
Repeated edits may reuse upstream results, so they do not establish fresh ColorField recomputation costs.
Actual grid, settings, geometry and cache policy are in matched workload keys. Catalog names do not establish resolution.
Physical footprint uses nominal100ms samples. These are observed trial maxima, not guaranteed transient peaks or settled physical memory.
Retained CPU/GPU/reserved inventories are logical ownership. They are not measured VRAM and must not be added to process footprint.
All initial and reversed observations remain separate. No favorable trial selection or automatic release clearance.
Raw reports and memory samples remain separate evidence. This compact summary is not a raw regression.json input to compare.py.

processing_output_evidence.reader_validation_scope: 125 Adobe SDK parse/decode checks with exact samples; not visual appearance approval.

concurrency.limits: Concurrent footprints size correctness capacity only. They are not release memory-regression observations.

setup_attempts: The initial combined-original Rust group passed 148 of 149 because a Merrill-only decoder test received mixed architectures. Its exact rerun with the pinned full-resolution Merrill fixture passed. The initial result remains retained.
A lost SSH connection interrupted orchestration after 42 GUI worker checks. Only the five remaining diagnostics checks were resumed, all passing.
Private Windows tests initially lacked pinned DXC DLLs beside compiler-reported test paths. Staging existing verified DLLs resolved setup failures.

The owner requested concurrent correctness. The 580 verified slider cases and first 38 catalog jobs were retained. Known 2 GiB guard deferrals and owner-interrupted attempts remain separate. Stable native and Python terminal records were audited before requeue. The final 1,440-case union checks native, session and image assertions, package/renderer identities and declared sources/recipes.
coverage_gaps: 154 ignored research, independent-golden or measurement cases remain excluded with input/measurement reasons.
Full Windows GUI/performance comparisons are unavailable with the current POSIX-dependent runner. The Windows 11 package passes native startup and rendering.
Windows 10 and native macOS 15 graphics/quarantine coverage remain unavailable. Hosted macOS 15 checks signed binary loading only.
The historical hosted parallel Windows native access violation remains unresolved. Serial passes do not establish a fix.
The acceptance inventory retains file-dialog, some preferences/restart, clipboard and recorder gaps. Passing 48 jobs is not complete user-path coverage.
Warm edits can reuse upstream processing. These observations do not establish cold process startup, screen scanout or fresh ColorField recomputation latency.
findings: All 12 catalog workflows, two enabled-feature workloads and three reversed confirmations have comparable workload identities. No automatic performance budget was applied.
The Draft edit p95 initially rose 16.440 ms with median +0.081 ms. Reversed trials instead changed median -0.132 ms and p95 -1.125 ms, consistent with scheduling variation.
HDR warm-edit median initially rose 0.823 ms and p95 36.428 ms. Reversed trials changed median -15.764 ms and p95 -6.931 ms. No consistent HDR slowdown was established.

Eight-photo exposure-edit median rose 13.542 ms initially and 12.519 ms in reversed trials, about 6%. Excluding the first slow edit in each trial still leaves roughly a 15 ms increase. This measures settled delivery to all eight targets. It is not per-photo or shader time. The p95 changed +1.27% initially and -0.21% in reversed trials. Retain the repeated narrow difference for owner review rather than calling it proven noise or a broad responsiveness regression.

Median sampled physical-footprint peak changes are HDR -0.38%, ColorField -7.06%, multi-photo -0.30% and native-detail +0.35%. No growth pattern was observed. Lower ColorField samples do not establish a code-caused optimization.
Correctness and exact package checks are complete. Publication still requires owner review of observations and release-specific decisions on remaining coverage gaps.
